messages.content: Front Range update before I book: Boulder moved exhibitor check-in earlier, Aurora moved the transfer fair into a campus building with pretty limited visitor parking, and Fort Collins confirmed a late-afternoon end. Can you rerank the flight and hotel plan? I’m worried the Thursday-night return is now too tight.

Yes. I’d keep the Tuesday afternoon nonstop as the easy piece, then downgrade the Thursday-night return. Ranking now: 1) Friday return from Denver: best reliability, because you can eat after Fort Collins, sleep near DEN, and handle rental return without sprinting. 2) Thursday night only if there is a very late nonstop and you are willing to skip a real dinner. 3) Thursday connection: I would not choose it for this loop. The risk is the Fort Collins-to-DEN drive plus rental return, bag/security, and a tired end of day.
That matches my gut. What about hotels—can I still avoid moving every night, or is that going to create worse mornings?

One base is possible, but each version hurts a different event. A Broomfield/Interlocken base helps Boulder and is decent for Fort Collins, but makes the Aurora campus morning longer and parking uncertainty worse. A DTC/Aurora base helps the transfer fair but makes the earlier Boulder check-in a pre-dawn drive. The least stressful working plan is split: Tuesday Broomfield/Interlocken, Wednesday Aurora or DTC, and then likely Thursday near DEN if you choose the Friday return. It is more packing, but the hotel changes follow the route instead of fighting it.
If Boulder availability is tightening, which Tuesday area should I target first?

Start with Broomfield/Interlocken, not central Boulder. It keeps the Boulder drive around 15–25 minutes without paying campus-event prices, and it has easier parking and dinner. Louisville or Superior is the backup if Broomfield jumps. I would avoid downtown Denver Tuesday because the earlier check-in makes that unnecessary stress.
For Wednesday, Aurora versus DTC? Parking worries me more than restaurant variety at this point.

Then lean Aurora/Anschutz if you can get a refundable rate with breakfast and parking that is not absurd. You’ll be closer for the morning setup and can scout the campus garage the night before. DTC is more comfortable for dinner, but it adds another variable on the one morning where parking is already constrained. Ask the host which garage exhibitors should use, whether there is an unload zone, and whether the visitor lot uses an app.
What drive-time risk should I respect most, especially with Fort Collins in the mix?

For Boulder, the risk is campus traffic and check-in moving earlier, so leave Broomfield with a 20-minute cushion. For Aurora, build in 15–20 minutes just for parking/payment, even if the hotel is close. For Fort Collins, do not leave Aurora hungry or right at the last possible minute; northbound traffic can look fine and then clog. I’d rather you arrive early and answer email in the car than eat the whole buffer on I-25.
Can you add breakfast and dinner backups and give me the clean ranking to use when I start holding rooms?

Clean plan: first, hold Tuesday in Broomfield/Interlocken with free parking and breakfast if available. Second, hold Wednesday in Aurora/Anschutz; use DTC only if Aurora rates are ugly. Third, hold Thursday near DEN if the Friday nonstop is reasonably priced, because it protects the airport morning. Food backups: Tuesday dinner near Broomfield/FlatIron Crossing; Wednesday do not rely entirely on the Boulder host breakfast, so bring a bar or yogurt and get coffee after setup; Wednesday dinner near Aurora/Anschutz or DTC depending on the hotel; Thursday eat lunch before leaving Aurora, then do a quick Fort Collins dinner after the meetup or fall back to Tower Road near the airport hotel. Flight ranking: Friday return first, late Thursday nonstop distant second, Thursday connection no.

messages.content: I’m ready to reserve the Front Range loop. Can you turn the split plan into actual booking choices? The only thing I’m still debating is whether Thursday night by the Denver airport is worth one more hotel change.

I’d keep the airport hotel. It changes the annoyance from packing one more time to sleeping close to the rental return, which is the safer trade. Before I lock the notes: refundable rates only, and are you okay with a single-bed room? Also, should I choose the comparable Delta nonstop if the fare is in line with United or Southwest?
Yes: refundable, single queen room is fine, Delta if it’s comparable, and please request window seats. If a non-Delta nonstop is much better, I don’t need Delta for the sake of it.

Then I’d use the Tuesday afternoon Delta nonstop SLC-DEN, arriving midafternoon, and the Friday early-afternoon Delta nonstop back to SLC. Both preserve the Tuesday handoff and avoid any connection risk. Request window seats now; if the exact window assignment is blocked, set a check-in reminder to try again when seats open.
The Friday return I’m seeing is 12:40. I can make that. What pickup and return times should I put on the rental car?

Set pickup for 30–45 minutes after scheduled Denver arrival, so you are not late on paper if bags take a bit. Return it Friday around 10:45 for the 12:40 flight. I’d book an intermediate car rather than compact because of materials and late-February Front Range weather. Keep the car the whole loop; rideshares would be too clumsy for Boulder, Aurora parking, and Fort Collins.
Okay. Hotel sequence and parking costs?

Tuesday: Broomfield/Interlocken, refundable, one queen requested, free parking, breakfast starting around 6:30, dinner options nearby. Wednesday: Aurora/Anschutz first choice, DTC only if the rate jumps; expect about $10–15 hotel parking and confirm the campus garage separately. Thursday: Denver airport/Tower Road area, breakfast from about 6:00, parking roughly $10–12. Choose flexible rates, not prepaid.
Is Aurora/Anschutz worth giving up DTC restaurants?

For this trip, yes. The transfer fair morning got more sensitive after the room move, and a 10-minute hotel-to-campus drive plus parking buffer is better than a prettier dinner area. You can still eat near the medical campus, go to Stanley Marketplace, or stop in DTC before checking in if you want something nicer.
And after Fort Collins? I don’t want to pull into the airport hotel starving.

Plan A is dinner in Fort Collins right after the meetup, even if it is counter-service. Leave town around 6:30–6:45 and you should reach the airport area without needing food there. Plan B is drive south first and use Tower Road near the hotel, but that can feel late. I’d put Fort Collins dinner on the calendar as part of the event wrap-up.
Great. Give me the reservation notes and receipt reminders.

Reservation set to enter: Delta SLC-DEN Tuesday afternoon and Delta DEN-SLC Friday 12:40, window seats requested both ways; intermediate rental car at DEN from Tuesday arrival to Friday 10:45 return; hotels Tuesday Broomfield/Interlocken, Wednesday Aurora/Anschutz, Thursday DEN airport/Tower Road, all refundable, one queen requested, breakfast verified where listed. Cancellation reminders: Broomfield by Monday 6 p.m., Aurora by Tuesday 6 p.m., airport hotel by Wednesday 6 p.m., assuming those are the flexible-rate terms shown before payment. Expense notes: save airfare receipt, rental estimate and final receipt, each hotel folio, campus or garage parking, fuel, and any baggage or materials fee separately.

messages.content: Eight days out: Boulder now wants us there by 6:55, Fort Collins sent a parking map with the west lot closed, and Delta moved the Friday return to 12:10. Flights, car, and the three hotels are booked. Can you tighten the timing instead of reopening the search?

Yes. Tuesday stays the same: land midafternoon, get the car, drive to Broomfield, eat nearby, and stage your materials. Wednesday, check out before leaving, put luggage in the trunk, depart about 6:10 for a 6:45–6:50 Boulder arrival. After Boulder, move south and check into Aurora/Anschutz. Thursday, check out before the fair, leave around 7:15, and aim to park by 7:40 for the 8:15 setup. After Aurora, have lunch before the Fort Collins drive.
So Wednesday breakfast at the hotel is probably not realistic?
Right. Treat it as coffee only unless they have grab-and-go out early. Buy yogurt or a bar Tuesday night, then use the Boulder event or a campus coffee stop after setup for the real breakfast.
For Thursday, do I leave everything in the car during Aurora and then drive straight north?

Yes. Put luggage and materials in the trunk before checkout, keep the smallest event bag with you, and do one quick car check after the fair before leaving. If the fair ends on time, lunch nearby first; if it runs long, take food to go and preserve at least a 90-minute drive buffer to Fort Collins.
What’s the Fort Collins move with the closed lot, and what’s my no-drama Friday airport schedule?

Use the primary garage on the new map, not the closed west lot, and arrive 35–40 minutes early. If the garage is full, drop materials at the building first, then use the overflow lot and walk back. Eat in Fort Collins after the meetup if you’re done around 5:30; otherwise grab food to go and head for the airport hotel. Friday: leave the hotel at 9:10–9:15, fuel on Tower Road, return the car by 9:45–10:00, and be at bag drop by 10:25 for the 12:10 flight. If the fuel line is bad, skip it and protect bag drop.
